pull.title: util: Add and use AssertUnreachable
pull.body:
The current code uses assertions with falsy literal values in a few places. This is perfectly fine, but this comes with a bit of confusion sometimes:

* `assert(false)` may cause confusion when it is unclear if `NDEBUG` can disable it. (The intention is to disallow `NDEBUG` compilation). Also, it can lead to warnings when used with clang-cl.exe (GCC seems to understand it)
* `Assert(false)` hides the noreturn attribute behind a function call, which may cause GCC return-type warnings. (Clang seems to understand it)

See https://godbolt.org/z/h7PT3jh3Y for the clang-cl/GCC warning reproducer.

* When C++23 will be allowed, devs may prefer `std::unreachable`. However, this is unsafe and will invoke UB.
* There is confusion why a `CHECK_NONFATAL` macro exists, but no fatal equivalent.

Fix all those issues by:

* Adding a new `AssertUnreachable`, which directly calls the noreturn `assertion_fail` helper.
* Adding an `assert_falsy` linter to enforce code to use this macro.

scripted-diff: Replace falsy assertions with AssertUnreachable

Replace assertions with falsy literal values by the explicit
unreachable-code assertion macro.

-BEGIN VERIFY SCRIPT-

 # Paths to edit.
 # Excluded are subtrees and modules that can not include util/check.
 paths=(
   'src'
   ':(exclude)src/script/interpreter.cpp'
   ':(exclude)src/tinyformat.h'
   ':(exclude)src/univalue/'
   ':(exclude)src/crc32c'
   ':(exclude)src/crypto/ctaes'
   ':(exclude)src/ipc/libmultiprocess'
   ':(exclude)src/leveldb'
   ':(exclude)src/minisketch'
   ':(exclude)src/secp256k1'
 )

 for f in $(git grep -l --extended-regexp '\<(a|A)ssert\((0|false)\)' -- "${paths[@]}"); do

   # Add the util/check.h includes
   if ! grep --quiet "util/check.h" "$f"; then
     line=$(grep --line-number --max-count=1 '^#include' "$f" | cut --delimiter=: --fields=1)
     sed --in-place "${line}i#include <util/check.h>" "$f"
   fi

   # Remove cassert includes
   sed --in-place '/^#include <cassert>$/d' "$f"

   # Sort includes
   git diff -U1 $f | ./contrib/devtools/clang-format-diff.py -p1 -i -v

   # Use AssertUnreachable
   sed --in-place --regexp-extended 's/\<(a|A)ssert\((0|false)\)/AssertUnreachable()/g' "$f"

 done

-END VERIFY SCRIPT-

comments.body: `AssertUnreachable` here and in `SignatureHashSchnorr` calls `assertion_fail` from `util/check.cpp`. This file is in `libbitcoin_consensus`, which should only depend on crypto. Normal builds hide it, `bitcoin_common` pulls util in anyway, but the riscv job links the lib standalone and breaks. Exclude consensus from `assert_falsy` under the same "not linking the util lib" reason, or move `assertion_fail`?

The message says any falsy literal, but the regex hardcodes the spacing, so `assert (false)`, `assert(false )` and `assert(0&&"x")` all slip through. `\<(a|A)ssert\s*\(\s*(0|false)\s*(&&|\))` catches them. And `std_unreachable` lets `__builtin_unreachable()` through. libstdc++ implements `std::unreachable()` as exactly that, and it builds under C++20 where `std::unreachable()` doesn't. Worth catching the builtin too?

The scripted-diff that satisfies this linter is the next commit, so lint is red here, 135 lines. Swapping the two applies cleanly and gives the same tree. The linters already in master came in with their fix in one commit.

> `\<(a|A)ssert\s*\(\s*(0|false)\s*(&&|\))`

Thx, used that.

> __builtin_unreachable

I think the risk of someone using it should be low, because it is a compiler-specific built-in.
Thx, will fix this some time before taking out of draft.

fa47891c9b8db91b055ccbbee0282c295a52deb0

The new message no longer mentions `assert`, but the regex still catches it.

fa3ec8d81d141019e7a5352aec8f067970a027d7

This header does not belong in this group.
